newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG NUG case sent to district court.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG NUG case sent to district court.

text.p: New York State Electric & Gas Corp said Tuesday a federal appeals court has rejected the utility's appeal of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's refusal to modify power purchase contracts with Saranac Power Partners LP and Lockport Energy Associates, L.P.
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit said NYSEG may pursue its claim against the owners of the power plants in U.S. District Court, the utility said.
It said the Saranac partnership is owned by CalEnergy Co Inc.
"We are pleased that the court did not grant the request of the owners of the nonutility generators (NUGs) to dismiss NYSEG's argument," the company said.
In 1996, NUG power cost more than $300 million and accounted for $0.185 out of every dollar of NYSEG's revenues.
The utility said it projects the mandated power purchases from the two plants will cost it some $2 billion more than the market, or "avoided," cost of the same amount of power.

NYSEG petitioned the FERC to modify these contracts in 1995, pointing out that payments under the contracts vastly exceed the avoided cost cap imposed by the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act (PURPA).
The power purchase contracts with the owners of the Plattsburgh and Lockport plants end in 2009 and 2007, respectively.
